headline: Law lets Cape Fox Corporation, an Alaska Native village corporation, finish its land claim using about 180 acres of Tongass National Forest land.
what_it_does: Cape Fox no longer has to take about 185 acres it had selected in the township around the village of Saxman, Alaska. Instead, it can choose land outside its current selection boundary to complete its remaining land entitlement. If Cape Fox sends written notice to the Interior Department within 90 days choosing about 180 acres of surface land in the Tongass National Forest, Interior must transfer that land. The underground rights go to Sealaska Corporation, and a public access easement is kept on the land.

who_it_affects.group: Cape Fox Corporation and its Alaska Native shareholders from Saxman
who_it_affects.how: They can receive about 180 acres of Tongass National Forest surface land in place of land they had selected near Saxman.
It receives the subsurface (underground) rights to the land conveyed to Cape Fox.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the public who use the Tongass National Forest
who_it_affects.how: The transferred land leaves federal ownership, but a public access easement is kept on it.
It must transfer the land if Cape Fox gives written notice within 90 days.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted May 19, 2026; Cape Fox has 90 days after enactment to send written notice of its selection.
